where: Section 3 (LMS), repeated in the figure and in the Exam traps
problem: The error is defined as e(n) = d(n) − â(n), where â(n) is called the decided output symbol. But the same section says decision-directed mode uses the receiver's own decision as d(n). If d(n) = â(n), then e(n) = 0 and the weights never update. A student following the text literally gets no adaptation in decision-directed mode.
fix: Define the error against the equaliser output before the slicer: e(n) = d(n) − y(n), where y(n) = Σk ck x(n−k) is the equaliser output sample at the decision instant. In training mode d(n) is the known training symbol; in decision-directed mode d(n) = â(n), the slicer output, so e(n) = â(n) − y(n). Keep the sign trap as 'd(n) − y(n), not y(n) − d(n)'.

problem: The error box note says 'd(n) − â(n)', which carries the same contradiction as Section 3: in decision-directed mode d(n) is the decision â(n).
fix: Change the note to 'd(n) − y(n)', where y(n) is the adder output before the threshold.

problem: The index and time notations are mixed: y(n) = c0x(n) + c1x(n−T), while everywhere else the stored sample is written x(n−k) with an integer lag k.
fix: Write y(n) = c0x(n) + c1x(n−1), i.e. the second tap is delayed by one symbol period T.

problem: The pointer to the Nyquist condition is written as plain text '5.1' with no cross-reference link, so on a phone the reader cannot jump to it.
fix: Make it a chapter link, e.g. Section 5.1 gives the Nyquist condition for zero ISI.
